\section[vidāya]{\kn{ವಿದಾಯ} (vidāya) — farewell}

\label{lesson:KA-C106-farewell}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for love, then the Kannada for appreciation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ವಿದಾಯ}}
\textbf{\kn{ವಿದಾಯ}} (\emph{vidāya}) — \textquotedblleft{}farewell\textquotedblright{}, a formal parting word for speeches and letters.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The formal goodbye.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vidāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vidāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{vidāya}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for love, then the Kannada for appreciation, then say \emph{vidāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ವಿದಾಯ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Farewell\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ivattu]{\kn{ಇವತ್ತು} (ivattu) — today}

\label{lesson:KA-C106-today}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for appreciation, then the Kannada for farewell.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಇವತ್ತು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಇವತ್ತು}} (\emph{ivattu}) — \textquotedblleft{}today\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ನಾಳೆ}} (\emph{nāḷe}) is \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The day before tomorrow.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ivattu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ivattu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ivattu}, then \emph{nāḷe}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for appreciation, then the Kannada for farewell, then say \emph{ivattu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಇವತ್ತು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Today\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nantara]{\kn{ನಂತರ} (nantara) — later, afterwards}

\label{lesson:KA-C106-later}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for farewell, then the Kannada for today.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ನಂತರ}}
\textbf{\kn{ನಂತರ}} (\emph{nantara}) — \textquotedblleft{}later, afterwards\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ಆಮೇಲೆ}} (\emph{āmēle}) says the same in everyday speech.

A second word for later.

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for farewell, then the Kannada for today, then say \emph{nantara} again

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[phōn māḍi]{\kn{ಫೋನ್} \kn{ಮಾಡಿ} (phōn māḍi) — please phone}

\label{lesson:KA-C106-phone}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for today, then the Kannada for later.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಫೋನ್} \kn{ಮಾಡಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಫೋನ್} \kn{ಮಾಡಿ}} (\emph{phōn māḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}please phone (me)\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}please do a phone\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ಮಾಡಿ}} is the polite form of \textbf{\kn{ಮಾಡು}}, \textquotedblleft{}do\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to stay in touch after goodbye.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phōn māḍi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phōn māḍi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{phōn māḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for today, then the Kannada for later, then say \emph{phōn māḍi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಫೋನ್} \kn{ಮಾಡಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please phone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[siguttēne]{\kn{ಸಿಗುತ್ತೇನೆ} (siguttēne) — I'll see you}

\label{lesson:KA-C106-seeyou}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for later, then the Kannada for please phone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸಿಗುತ್ತೇನೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸಿಗುತ್ತೇನೆ}} (\emph{siguttēne}) — \textquotedblleft{}I'll see you\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}I will be met\textquotedblright{}. It is the same verb as \textbf{\kn{ಸಿಗೋಣ}} (\emph{sigōṇa}), \textquotedblleft{}let's meet\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಾಳೆ} \kn{ಸಿಗುತ್ತೇನೆ}} (\emph{nāḷe siguttēne}) — \textquotedblleft{}I'll see you tomorrow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The last word of the tranche: a promise to meet.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{siguttēne}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{siguttēne}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nāḷe siguttēne}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for later, then the Kannada for please phone, then say \emph{siguttēne} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಸಿಗುತ್ತೇನೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}I'll see you\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Out and about — a first pass}

\label{lesson:KA-R106-first-pass-moods-body-find}



\begin{quote}
Ask a friend to phone you, and promise to see them tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item name boredom, enthusiasm, shyness, alarm and peace of mind
  \item take a breath; name skin and blood; say you have a stomach ache; ask someone's weight
  \item ask for the map and one ticket; ask where the bus stop is; ask if it is near
  \item please open the door; please close it; please stop here; please call the doctor; it's urgent!
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Boredom? (\textbf{\kn{ಬೇಸರ}}.) Enthusiasm? (\textbf{\kn{ಉತ್ಸಾಹ}}.) Shyness? (\textbf{\kn{ನಾಚಿಕೆ}}.) Alarm? (\textbf{\kn{ಗಾಬರಿ}}.) Peace of mind? (\textbf{\kn{ನೆಮ್ಮದಿ}}.) Breath, skin, blood? (\textbf{\kn{ಉಸಿರು}, \kn{ಚರ್ಮ}, \kn{ರಕ್ತ}}.) Stomach ache? (\textbf{\kn{ಹೊಟ್ಟೆನೋವು}}.) Weight? (\textbf{\kn{ತೂಕ}}.) Map, ticket, bus, station? (\textbf{\kn{ನಕ್ಷೆ}, \kn{ಟಿಕೆಟ್}, \kn{ಬಸ್}, \kn{ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ}}.) Near? (\textbf{\kn{ಹತ್ತಿರ}}.) Open, close, stop, call? (\textbf{\kn{ತೆರೆಯಿರಿ}, \kn{ಮುಚ್ಚಿ}, \kn{ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ}, \kn{ಕರೆಯಿರಿ}}.) Urgent? (\textbf{\kn{ತುರ್ತು}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Home, work and the road — a second pass}

\label{lesson:KA-R106-second-pass-home-work-wishes}



\begin{quote}
Tell someone about your home and the street it is on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item I want a different one; I made a mistake; everything is fine; only one; for no reason
  \item name your city, your country and a state
  \item name business, a worker, the police, a driver and a shop
  \item festival greetings; thank a host for their hospitality; name love and appreciation
  \item farewell; today; later; please phone; I'll see you tomorrow
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Other? (\textbf{\kn{ಬೇರೆ}}.) Wrong? (\textbf{\kn{ತಪ್ಪು}}.) All? (\textbf{\kn{ಎಲ್ಲಾ}}.) Only one? (\textbf{\kn{ಒಂದೇ}}.) For no reason? (\textbf{\kn{ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ}}.) House, street, city, country, state? (\textbf{\kn{ಮನೆ}, \kn{ಬೀದಿ}, \kn{ನಗರ}, \kn{ದೇಶ}, \kn{ರಾಜ್ಯ}}.) Business, worker, police, driver, shop? (\textbf{\kn{ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ}, \kn{ಕೆಲಸಗಾರ}, \kn{ಪೊಲೀಸ್}, \kn{ಚಾಲಕ}, \kn{ಅಂಗಡಿ}}.) Best wishes? (\textbf{\kn{ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು}}.) Festival? (\textbf{\kn{ಹಬ್ಬ}}.) Hospitality? (\textbf{\kn{ಆತಿಥ್ಯ}}.) Love? (\textbf{\kn{ಪ್ರೀತಿ}}.) Appreciation? (\textbf{\kn{ಮೆಚ್ಚುಗೆ}}.) Farewell? (\textbf{\kn{ವಿದಾಯ}}.) Today? (\textbf{\kn{ಇವತ್ತು}}.) Later? (\textbf{\kn{ನಂತರ}}.) Please phone? (\textbf{\kn{ಫೋನ್} \kn{ಮಾಡಿ}}.) I'll see you? (\textbf{\kn{ಸಿಗುತ್ತೇನೆ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
